taxonomyDefinition.counting: occurrenceCount counts every diagnostic instance across all 160 cases; caseCount counts distinct cases; functionCount counts distinct (case, function name, address) triples implicated via the reconstruction line map

clusters.title: undeclared global data symbol (global_<addr>)
clusters.producerLayer: global symbol rendering (data symbol table -> declarations)
clusters.description: Global data referenced by address is rendered as an identifier the TU never declares. Required metadata is a global symbol declaration block.

clusters.title: C++ mangled symbol emitted as a C identifier and never declared
clusters.description: Mangled C++ names (_Z.../Z...) are emitted verbatim as C identifiers and called without a prototype. Distinct from A-MISSING-PROTOTYPE because the identifier itself is not a valid C-symbol contract.

representative.message: implicit declaration of function 'Z_tst64' is invalid in C99 [-Wimplicit-function-declaration]

clusters.title: missing external function prototype (sub_<addr> and named callees)
clusters.producerLayer: function prototype rendering / TU ownership boundary
clusters.description: Calls to functions defined later in the same TU, or never defined, reach the compiler with no prototype (implicit declaration; C99-invalid, an error from clang 16 / gcc 14 onward).

representative.message: implicit declaration of function 'sub_8E0' is invalid in C99 [-Wimplicit-function-declaration]

clusters.title: undeclared user/engine type name
clusters.description: Names such as vector128, Base, Derived, Container, std are used as type names or in cast position with no type declaration in the TU.

clusters.title: non-standard integer type alias (uint32 / uint64 / int64 / uint8)
clusters.producerLayer: type alias rendering (bare alias names instead of typedefs)
clusters.description: Type names are emitted as bare uint32/uint64/int64/uint8, which are not C types. Both `unknown type name` in declaration position and `use of undeclared identifier` in cast position are this same producer gap.

clusters.title: undeclared decompiler runtime / pseudo-intrinsic helper
clusters.description: The printer emits helper calls (unknown_call, phi, bit_extract, bit_insert, sext, __a64_movi_*, __arm64_condition_*, __arm64_nzcv_*) as if a runtime header declared them. No such declaration is emitted in the TU.

representative.message: implicit declaration of function 'unknown_call' is invalid in C99 [-Wimplicit-function-declaration]

clusters.title: standard fixed-width alias used without <stdint.h>
clusters.producerLayer: type alias rendering / missing standard header emission
clusters.description: uint32_t / uint64_t / int32_t are used, but the TU includes no header and no typedef. Correct spelling, missing declaration.

clusters.title: call argument count contradicts an emitted zero-arg declaration
clusters.description: Call sites pass arguments while another emitted (void) declaration of the same name claims zero parameters.

representative.message: too many arguments to function call, expected 0, have 1

clusters.title: same emitted symbol defined more than once
clusters.description: Placeholder names ($x) and parameter-resolved names are reused, producing `redefinition of 'X'`.

clusters.title: entry point rendered with a non-int return type
clusters.description: The emitted `main` does not have type `int ()`, so clang warns with -Wmain-return-type. A signature-rendering defect, not a missing declaration.

clusters.title: later definition conflicts with an earlier implicit declaration
clusters.description: A call before the definition creates an implicit `int f()` declaration; the later `void f(void)` definition then conflicts. Root cause is the missing forward prototype, surfaced as a type conflict.

clusters.title: declaration with incomplete type
clusters.description: Invalid declarators (C++ qualified names) parse as a variable of type `void`, producing `variable has incomplete type 'void'`.

clusters.title: invalid C declarator name (C++ qualified / demangled names)
clusters.description: Names such as `thunk to MultiDerived::funcB` or `Container::get` are emitted as C declarators, producing `expected ';' after top level declarator` and `variable has incomplete type 'void'`.

clusters.title: member access on a non-struct base (dotted symbol names)
clusters.description: Names like `param_atomic_ops.constprop.0` are emitted as C identifiers; `.` parses as member access on a function name.

representative.message: member reference base type 'void (void)' is not a structure or union

clusters.title: label emitted before the function body compound statement
clusters.description: A `loc_<hex>:` label is emitted between the declarator and the opening brace: `uint64 f(void)\n  loc_9A0:\n{`. Invalid at file scope; the label belongs inside the body.

representative.message: expected function body after function declarator

clusters.title: malformed expression caused by an undeclared type name
clusters.description: `*(uint64 *)0x13FD0` fails as `expected expression` because uint64 is not a declared type. This is a downstream cascade, not an independent defect.

clusters.title: statement emitted outside any function body
clusters.description: A `goto loc_<hex>;` is emitted after the function's closing brace, at file scope, producing `expected identifier or '('`.

clusters.title: string literal combined with arithmetic instead of concatenation
clusters.description: `"literal" + i` is emitted where C requires indexing; clang warns that adding to a string does not append.

representative.message: adding 'int' to a string does not append to the string [-Wstring-plus-int]

clusters.title: undeclared raw architecture register (sp, lr, pc)
clusters.description: sp/lr/pc are emitted as C identifiers.

clusters.title: undeclared parameter/return pseudo-variable (a1, a2, v0, ...)
clusters.producerLayer: function signature rendering vs body variable rendering
clusters.description: The emitted signature does not declare the parameters the body uses (e.g. `void f(void)` whose body reads a1, a2, a3), so argument pseudo-variables are undeclared.

clusters.title: undeclared generated call temporary (call_<n>)
clusters.producerLayer: temporary generation inside the body emitter
clusters.description: Per-call result temporaries are generated and consumed without ever being declared. Pure body-scoped temporaries.

clusters.title: undeclared condition temporary (condition_*)
clusters.description: Condition temporaries (condition_eq, condition_hi, condition_le, ...) are referenced without declaration.

clusters.title: goto to a label the emitted body never defines
clusters.description: `goto loc_<hex>;` references a label that is not present in the emitted function, so the control-flow structuring and label emission disagree.

clusters.title: undeclared SSA phi temporary (local_phi_*)
clusters.description: SSA phi temporaries are emitted as identifiers rather than being lowered into declared locals.

clusters.title: undeclared register pseudo-variable (x0, x19, w0, d0, ...)
clusters.description: Raw architecture register names (x0, x0_1, x19, w0, d0, q0) escape into the body as ordinary identifiers without declaration.

clusters.title: undeclared stack-slot / local-memory pseudo-variable
clusters.description: local_<off>, local_p<hex>, var_<off>, field_<off> are used as lvalues and rvalues inside the function body with no local declaration. These are body-scoped and are not TU-level packaging gaps.

clusters.title: undeclared value/return pseudo-variable (v0, v165, v1010, ...)
clusters.description: SSA value indices are emitted with a `v` prefix (v165, v1010) and used as operands with no declaration. Shares the spelling space with ARM64 SIMD registers v0..v31.

clusters.title: unresolved operand emitted as a literal `?` token
clusters.description: A statement is emitted with `?` in operand position (e.g. `? = *(uint64 *)(x1);`), producing `expected ':'`. A printer placeholder escapes into the output as a token instead of a value.

clusters.title: parser recovery diagnostic caused by an earlier undeclared type
clusters.description: `expected ']'` and similar recovery errors. All 34 `expected ']'` occurrences are on lines that also contain an undeclared int alias, so this is measurement noise from the type-alias gap, not a separate bug.

clusters.title: compiler note attached to a parent diagnostic
clusters.description: clang `note:` diagnostics. They add evidence to a parent error but are not separate defects.

clusters.title: unclassified diagnostic
clusters.description: Diagnostic not matched by any deterministic cluster rule.

clusters.title: environment / toolchain only
clusters.description: Timeout, missing compiler, or non-source diagnostic.
